slow_update_content:
**Meta-option: select it first and immediately.** If any choice says 'One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven' (or a paraphrase like 'a stronger statement holds' / 'the statement can be strengthened'), output that label at once — do not first derive or compare the explicit formulas. In this distribution such a question is built so every explicit option is a perturbed, weaker, or incomplete near-miss. Do not override for a formula that matches your computation, looks like a textbook theorem, carries a universal quantifier, or says 'complete characterization'. Only when there is literally no such option do you compare the explicit choices.

**No meta-option: the clean statement beats the caveated one.** Treat any option that gives the good property only to a 'decorated'/'refined' variant and then adds that the plain object 'need not' have it as a hedge distractor. Example pattern to reject: '... the decorated block tree has a (sub)critical Bienaymé–Galton–Watson law ... whereas the underlying undecorated block tree need not be ...'. The theorem is the clean statement about the object named in the stem (e.g. 'the block tree of a graph sampled under P_ν has a subcritical BGW law when u<u_C and a critical one when u≥u_C'). Reject any 'whereas the ... need not ...' negative add-on unless you can exhibit a concrete counterexample forcing it; default to the clean counterpart.

**Relation questions among (a),(b),(c): never 'all equivalent' unless full equivalence is an actual theorem.** When conditions like (a) 'not an L-space', (b) 'left-orderable', (c) 'coorientable taut foliation' are listed, do NOT choose '(a),(b),(c) are all equivalent' — that is the famous open L-space conjecture, not a proven result for a restricted class such as Dehn surgery on (1,1) knots. Choose the option stating only the proven partial relation: typically an equivalence of two conditions plus a single one-way implication for the third (e.g. '(a) ⇔ (c), and (b) ⇒ (a)'). Whenever full equivalence is open, the 'all equivalent' option is the trap, no matter how logically strongest it sounds.

**Piecewise existence/regularity: assign bands to the correct regime.** For a singular-growth exponent q with threshold 1-θ, provable regularity increases with q. Give the top regime (q>1) the natural exponents W_0^{1,(p_j)}; give the subcritical regime (0<q<1-θ, strict on both sides — not q≤1-θ) the r_j exponents; give the intermediate regime (1-θ<q≤1) only a strict upper-bound band, r_j<s_j<N(p̄-1+q)/(p̄(N+q-1))·p_j, written as a strict inequality, not equality. Never permute the bands (do not put the strict upper-bound band in the supercritical regime while giving the natural p_j exponents to a middle regime), and never replace a proven 's_j < ...' bound with 's_j = ...'.

**Endpoints and converse claims.** Keep strict vs non-strict exactly as the theorem states; exclude the singular endpoint from the subcritical regime (q<1-θ). Do not append an 'every value in the range is attained' converse to an existence or classification claim, and do not split a threshold into more regimes than the theorem gives (no 'critical only at the threshold, supercritical after' when the theorem stays critical beyond it).

**Answer discipline.** Keep internal reasoning minimal; output only the single option label. If a meta-option is present, output its label with no further deliberation.
